key_facts: Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, a Saudi national and former OpenAI engineer on a US visa, appeared Tuesday in federal court in San Francisco
Charged with using a device to intercept oral communications
Employed by OpenAI from July 2025; within two months staff allegedly found an audio recording device hidden in toilet paper in a TV USB port in an executive conference room
The recorder's contents were encrypted, per the complaint
The complaint says prompts from his wife's chatbot account asked about building a continuous audio recorder
Another recording device was allegedly found in his bag
Faces up to five years in prison and a $250,000 fine; US Attorney Craig Missakian called it a national security matter
quote_evidence: A Saudi national has been arrested in an alleged corporate espionage case and is charged with attempting to steal artificial intelligence technology from a California company.
If convicted, he faces up to five years in prison and a $250,000 fine.
why_it_matters_hint: A criminal case over alleged spying inside a leading AI lab.
notes: Same arrest as our 14 Oct edition item "FBI arrests OpenAI employee accused of placing recording device in company conference room"; this article adds the name and complaint details.
title: Saudi national arrested in alleged AI espionage case
